cards.text: Friend, Babylon has carried Judah off into exile (2 Kings 25:21). But Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon left some people behind in the land of Judah, and somebody has to be over them. He picks Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan.

cards.question: All the commanders of the armies hear the news: the king of Babylon has appointed Gedaliah as ___.

cards.text: So the commanders and their men come to see Gedaliah at Mizpah, and four of those commanders get named. I bet that first meeting was TENSE, like the first staff meeting after your company gets bought out: everybody smiling, NOBODY blinking.

cards.question: Which of these men is one of the commanders who come to Gedaliah at Mizpah?

cards.text: Then Gedaliah takes an oath in front of the commanders and all their men. Not a pep talk, friend. An OATH.

cards.question: In his oath, what does Gedaliah tell the commanders not to be afraid of?
In his oath, Gedaliah assures the commanders: live in the land and serve the king of ___, and it will be well with you.

cards.text: Sounds like things might finally calm down. Then in the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, a member of the royal family, shows up with ten men.

cards.question: Ishmael and his ten men come to Gedaliah at Mizpah. What does Ishmael do?
Ishmael kills Gedaliah but spares everyone who was with him at Mizpah.

cards.text: Babylon's governor is gone. Then all the people, small and great, get up and run, and the army commanders go right along with them.

cards.question: The people and the army commanders flee to Egypt.
Why do the people and the army commanders flee to Egypt?

answers.text: They are afraid of the Chaldeans
They are following the king of Egypt
They are running from a famine

cards.text: Now we go to Babylon, where Jehoiachin, the king of Judah carried off there years before (2 Kings 24:15), sits in prison in the thirty-seventh year of his exile. THIRTY-SEVEN YEARS, friend, and I get antsy when the oven timer has two minutes left.

cards.question: In the year Evil-merodach becomes king of Babylon, what does he do for Jehoiachin?

answers.text: He sends him back to Judah

cards.text: Evil-merodach speaks kindly to Jehoiachin, and there are other kings with Jehoiachin in Babylon too. A KIND word from Babylon's king after thirty-seven years? I'd make him say it twice, real slow.

cards.question: Evil-merodach sets Jehoiachin's throne below the thrones of the other kings with him in Babylon.

cards.text: So Jehoiachin changes out of his prison clothes. When I got out of the junk drawer, I left a whole coat of dust behind, and friend, I did NOT go back for it.

cards.question: Jehoiachin eats at the king's table just once, as a one-time honor.
On top of a seat at his table, the king gives Jehoiachin a daily ___ for the rest of his life.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Evil-merodach speaks kindly to Jehoiachin, and there are other kings with Jehoiachin in Babylon too." / "A KIND word from Babylon's king after thirty-seven years?" / "I'd make him say it twice, real slow." Only the opening card may run to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card runs to three sentences: "Then Gedaliah takes an oath in front of the commanders and all their men." / "Not a pep talk, friend." / "An OATH." Only the opening card may have 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The Chaldeans first appear in this card's right answer, and no card says who they are. They are the Babylonians. Without that, the baker can't reason from the setup (Babylon conquered Judah and appointed Gedaliah) to "the servants of the Chaldeans." A baker who doesn't know the name has to guess. The same gap affects card 13's right answer.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: No card tells the baker that Ishmael killed Judeans and Chaldeans along with Gedaliah at Mizpah (2 Kings 25:25). Card 10 only says Ishmael didn't spare everyone who was with Gedaliah. This detail explains why the people flee "for fear of the Chaldeans" (25:26). Without it, the baker misses an important detail, and card 13's "why" question has less to reason from.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
